---
title: "about"
subtitle: "What the FAIRtools framework is and why it exists"
---

The **FAIRtools framework** is a project funded by the [NWO](https://www.nwo.nl/en) Thematic Digital Competence Centre for Life Sciences & Health (**TDCC-LSH**). Its goal is to help researchers and research software engineers make their software **FAIR**: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable.

## Why research software

Research software is a scientific output in its own right. Analyses, papers, and datasets depend on it, yet much of it is hard to find, hard to install, missing a license, or impossible to tie to the exact version that produced a result. None of that is usually deliberate. Most research software is written by researchers under time pressure, and the practices that make software reusable are rarely part of their training.

The FAIR principles were originally written for data. Applying them to software means turning them into concrete, everyday practices: where to put the code, how to test and document it, how to package and release it, and how to make it easy to cite.

## What the project does

The project works on two fronts.

**A practical guide.** The [uplifting guide](uplifting.qmd) breaks the FAIR principles down into ten areas of practice, from repositories and testing to interoperability and citations. Each topic explains what to change and why it matters. The [checklist](checklist.qmd) condenses all ten topics into a quick self-assessment.

**Hands-on activities.** The guide grew out of the preparation for events organised by the project, and those events remain a core part of it. They range from [licensing outreach](activities/1licensing_outreach.qmd) to hackathons where developers bring their own tools to platforms such as [SURF Research Cloud](activities/2surf_research_hackathon.qmd) and [Galaxy](activities/4Galaxy_hackathon.qmd). See [activities](activities.qmd) for the full overview.

## Who it is for

The material is written for **researchers who write code** and for **research software engineers** who support them. You don't need to be a professional developer to use it. Each topic starts from a familiar problem and works toward a practical fix, so you can pick the ones that matter for your software and skip the rest.

## Contributing

This website is open source and built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Suggestions, corrections, and additions are welcome through the project's [GitHub repository](https://github.com/fair-toolbox/framework).
